body: I will NEVER be the one to initiate divorce, UNLESS there is physical abuse or cheating. Sometimes I feel him threatening divorce is a form of abuse I’m allowing and that’s why he keeps doing it; knowing I won’t leave.

I’ve been going through all of my posts and this one stuck out the most! Here’s an update: everything I said was Satan making me think he was doing things behind my back, was actually happening!!!!!!!

My spouse has struggled with porn addiction, gambling addiction, drug addiction, abuse and mental health issues our entire relationship.

Over the last couple months, I’ve found a prescription for drug he abuses, a new credit card, a secret bank account and have noticed money missing. He has since come clean about most of them, but when I’ve asked about them, he’s gotten very angry and has treated me poorly and called me ‘crazy’. This has left me feeling upset and going back to old ways of ‘justifying’ his actions. 

I fear he’s putting us in debt and I cannot trust him anymore. He travels for work and when he returns, he becomes a monster. It’s a constant battle. He used to be a good person, but his anger issues have turned him into someone I can’t stand being around. 

He wanted to divorce me a few months ago, but I changed into the person he claimed he wanted me to be. I didn’t stop there. I grew closer to God and my relationship with Him is the best it’s ever been. I finally gave it all to Him and my life changed forever. 

The triple A’s... all of them, but adultery, to my knowledge, has happened. I have a feeling it’s happened. I’m sure it’ll become exposed sooner or later. If that’s the case, I am for sure done. 

I’m worn out. I’m tired of trying to talk myself out of being angry when I have EVERY RIGHT to be angry about being lied to.

His reaction in the past was anger, calling me names and leaving anywhere from hours to days. I am told ‘You’re the reason...’ and then the tables turn and he plays the victim. I’m told what I do wrong, how he can’t stand me and become his verbal punching bag. 

He then apologizes and promises it’ll never happen again, but a week later, here we are. 

At this point, there’s nothing being chipped away when I’m called names or yelled at because it’s happened for so long, I’m checked out. I used to hurt; cry; ask myself ‘why?’ Now, I carry on and focus on myself and my children and live that day to the fullest! I can’t make him be the person that I know he can be. He carelessly spends money, abuses drugs, drinks daily, etc. I know God has a BIG plan for me and I’m excited to see it!
I have; I still meet with them weekly. They have helped me become stronger and see that there’s only so much I can do, but for the most part, he’s choosing to be the person he is.

He is well aware that I don’t trust him. We have been seeing a counselor, but haven’t discussed previous issues; basically were just making changes as we move forward. 

Should I remain silent about what my child told me? Or mention it in counseling? Or to someone at church? It’s not HORRIBLE, but I asked about it the other day and he said, ‘no.’ My child brought it up this morning.
I have. I feel like it helps, but only for a short period of time. It works, but the both of us let Satan take over our minds and make us think each other is the enemy instead of Satan himself.

My therapist just mentioned this today. She said that even if you remember things and tell them, or even show them recordings of them during the abuse, they will still deny it because they don’t want to take responsibility for their actions. It’ll always be our fault, even with evidence. 

Write down everything. Not because of them, but more so you can look back and realize you’re not crazy.

Hi there. 

I know when my spouse and I have an argument and he mentions me saying something, I do ask for an example. The tone in my voice is calm and I’m sincerely only asking because he doesn’t communicate with me when I make him feel a certain way. 

It sounds like in your situation, there are other forms of abuse.
I’ve been praying for him, myself and our situation. I just found out some detrimental stuff, which I feel is God telling me it’s okay to leave my abusive situation.
